title: Split the Word
goal: The first word of any sentence — as a view. Hardcoding is not splitting.
hints: &s[0..4] happens to work for 'rust'. The second test sends a different sentence.
split() yields subslices of the input — the first one IS the answer, no copy needed.
explanation: The hardcoded range compiles and even passes for the right four-letter word — then 'hi there' returns 'hi t' and the test objects: indexes encode assumptions, splitting encodes intent. split(' ').next() hands back a subslice of the original — a zero-copy view whose lifetime elision ties it to the input. The .to_owned() variant doesn't even compile here: the signature promises a borrowed &str, and returning an owned String breaks that promise (E0308).
